A 54-year-old male with atrial fibrillation on warfarin therapy is brought to the emergency department
with altered mental status. Two days prior, he had visited the ED for severe epistaxis that was
managed with nasal packing. Current vital signs show: temperature 98.4°F (36.4°C), blood pressure
83/53 mmHg, heart rate 160/min, respiratory rate 41/min, and oxygen saturation 100% on room air.
The patient is obtunded and unresponsive to questions. Physical examination reveals a dark, purpuric
rash on his trunk and extremities. Upon removal of the nasal packing, no active bleeding is observed.
After initiating IV fluids and obtaining blood cultures, which medication should be administered as the
first priority? Answer Choices: (A) IV corticosteroids (B) Ceftriaxone (C) Vancomycin (D) Vitamin K (E)
Amphotericin B (F) Penicillin (G) Clindamycin (H) Piperacillin-tazobactam (I) Meropenem (J) Fresh

frozen plasma
 A. Clindamycin
B. Penicillin
C. IV corticosteroids
D. Fresh frozen plasma
E. Vitamin K
F. Amphotericin B
G. Vancomycin
H. Meropenem
I. Piperacillin-tazobactam
J. Ceftriaxone
